newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia corn prices firm on Thai import quota.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia corn prices firm on Thai import quota.

text.p: Corn prices in Malaysia were set to soar this week on talk that Thai consumers were looking for substantial volumes of the staple from Kuala Lumpur to fulfill an import quota, dealers said on Tuesday.
The near 13 percent fall of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar in the last month was also keeping prices firm, dealers said.

Thailand, once a net maize exporter and now a net importer, has licenced the purchase of 150,000 tonnes of tariff-free corn between July and end-August after supply was found to be acutely short this year.
The country had allowed tariff-free import of another 200,000 tonnes earlier in the year, which was snapped up immediately.
Grains dealers in Malaysia said on Monday that the market in Kuala Lumpur was excited about the Thai import quota.
"I believe there has been some diversion of local stocks to Thailand already, but I'm not sure of the quantity," said a trader at a Malaysian flour mill.
In Thailand, importers were resisting the government's offer to bring in maize duty-free due to the "extremely short" time given to the industry to source the staple, sources said.
They said goods sourced in a hurry usually carried a premium and in the case of maize, the appreciation might be too much as domestic prices were already high.

About 75,000 tonnes, or half of the import quota, had already been exhausted, although it was doubtful that the balance could be met, said the sources. They added that the biggest buyer was Thai poultry giant CP.
Thailand produces between 4.3 and 4.5 million tonnes of corn annually and uses all of it on its domestic feed mill and poultry operations.
Maize stocks at warehouses in central Malaysia had steadily decreased from last month's level of more than 150,000 tonnes to about 60,000 to 70,000 tonnes this week, said dealers in Malaysia.
Dealers said overzealous buying and untimely arrival of fresh supplies were the basic reasons for the earlier maize glut in Kuala Lumpur.
They said the market was "talking" of pricing both Chinese and Argentine maize out of Kuala Lumpur at around 400 ringgit next week.
"It's just talk but it might happen. Of course, the currency is a factor, not just the Thai situation," said a dealer.
Bulk corn of Chinese origin in Malaysia's central region was quoted at between 375 and 380 ringgit ($134-$136) a tonne C and F this week, compared to 365-370 ringgit a week ago.
Bulk Argentine maize, ex-factories/godowns in the central region, was at 380 to 385 ringgit compared to 370-375 last week.
Wheat prices remained steady this week, on a thin trading volume, while soymeal rates were up slightly on a shortage of soybeans in the market, said another flour company official.
"A" grade wheat in Malaysia was at 650 ringgit a bag while "B" grade wheat was at 430 ringgit.
Local soymeal was at 885 ringgit compared to 865 ringgit last week, while the imported material was at 865 compared to 845 previously.
